paragraphs: In the morning, map critical-process dependencies with business and IT teams and identify single points of failure. At midday, write or revise plans, assigning recovery objectives and responsibilities. In the afternoon, run a tabletop exercise that forces teams to practice recovery from network and system outages. Before leaving, record exercise findings for the next review.

Work includes risk identification, plan writing, exercise facilitation, preparedness implementation, documentation maintenance, and incident response. It combines analytical work with coordination as the foundation of organizational resilience.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 1,205,700 business continuity planners were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to increase to 1,242,000 by 2034, a net gain of about 36,300 jobs, with approximately 108,200 openings each year. Median annual pay is about $81,300 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Business Continuity Planners and can make the occupation more stable. AI assists risk assessment and documentation, while people design plans, mobilize departments, organize exercises, and command incidents. Compliance places the greatest value on these human responsibilities.

The relatively high AI-exposure rating reflects extensive automation potential in risk scoring and document work. People retain plan design and organizational mobilization, while stronger compliance supports role stability.

Relatively high exposure does not mean high risk. AI replaces documentation and scoring tasks, not the role of building organizational resilience. People with strong mobilization and exercise experience are more secure.
Begin in management or IT and practice communication and project management. Pure document work is shrinking in the AI era, so build mobilization ability early.
Progress from writing plans to managing exercises and implementation. Learn business dependencies and compliance.
Emphasize exercise and recovery outcomes and identify the critical services you supported.
Do not hire on credentials alone. Assess whether candidates can mobilize departments and run realistic exercises.
